'ISANG MALAKING KAHIHIYAN'

Humarap kay NAPOLCOM Chief Atty. Vicente Calinisan ang pulis na sangkot sa sumingit na PNP-marked vehicle sa EDSA Busway sa Quezon City at nakabanggaan ng isang pampasaherong bus.

Ikinuwento ng bus driver na si Jessie Soledad sa NAPOLCOM ang mga pangyayari kaugnay ng aksidente at humingi naman ng pasensiya si Police Chief Master Sgt. Jenifer Bredico. Nabatid na kukuha ng pasahero para sa libreng sakay ang pulis kaya pumasok sa EDSA busway.

Ayon naman kay Calinisan, nagsasagawa na sila ng motu proprio investigation laban kay Chief Master Sgt. Jenifer Bredico. Isang malaking kahihiyan daw ang ginawa ng alagad ng batas. | via @_iancruz

data.text:
Ininspeksiyon ni DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon ngayong araw, April 20, ang Matalahib Creek Pumping Station sa Quezon City kasama sina Quezon City Mayor Joy Belmonte at UP Project Noah Executive Director Dr. Mahar Lagmay.

Noong 2024 pa raw itinayo ang pumping station pero hanggang ngayon, hindi pa rin ito gumagana. Itinayo raw ito nang walang pahintulot ng QC LGU at naiwang nakatengga nang dalawang taon.

Ayon sa QC LGU, imbis na maibsan ang problema sa baha sa mga kalapit na barangay, pinapalala pa raw nito ang sitwasyon lalo na kapag tag-ulan.

Target nila matapos ito sa Mayo pero ang pondo para maging operational itong pumping station, sa 2027 pa raw maipapasok dahil sa mga tapyas sa pondo ng DPWH para sa flood control ngayong taon. | via @beypinlac

data.text:
🚨 The United States is conducting military exercises with the Philippines despite being engaged in war against Iran

Thousands of U.S. and Filipino troops began annual military exercises on Monday, despite Washington’s involvement in war in the Middle East. For the first time this year, a Japanese military contingent has also joined.

The drills include live-fire exercises taking place in northern areas overlooking the Taiwan Strait, as well as in a province facing the disputed South China Sea, where tensions between Philippine and Chinese naval forces are ongoing.

Colonel Dennis Hernandez, spokesperson for the participating Philippine forces, said that the Japanese military, contributing 1,400 troops, will use a Type 88 cruise missile to sink a ship off the northern coast of Bawui.

More than 17,000 soldiers, airmen, and sailors are participating in the “Balikatan” exercises—meaning “shoulder to shoulder”—over a period of 19 days, roughly the same number as last year, including forces from Australia, New Zealand, France, and Canada.

U.S. military spokesperson Colonel Robert Pan described the exercises as an opportunity to showcase the strong alliance with the Philippines and demonstrate commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific region.

He confirmed that the number of U.S. forces involved—described as one of the largest deployments in years—has not been affected by the war in the Middle East, declining to provide exact figures.

The “Balikatan” exercises come as a ceasefire between Iran, the United States, and its ally Israel is nearing its end, having temporarily halted the war in the Middle East.

The conflict has led to a global energy crisis, significantly impacting the Philippines, which relies heavily on imports.

The exercises also take place amid rising Chinese military pressure around Taiwan, which Beijing considers part of its territory and has repeatedly threatened to take by force.

Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos said last November that due to his country’s proximity to the self-governing island, “a war over Taiwan would inevitably drag the Philippines into the conflict.”

Marcos considers the 1951 Mutual Defense Treaty between Manila and Washington a cornerstone of national security and has been strengthening security ties with Western countries to deter China.

Over the past two years, Manila has signed military agreements with Japan, New Zealand, Canada, and France to facilitate participation in joint exercises in the Philippines.

(AFP)
